children: Mortgage Bankers Association's Composite Index decreased 2.7% to 240.6 during the week ended September 4, compared to +0.8% to 247.3 seen in the prior week, according to the Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey.
The Market Composite Index is a measure of mortgage loan application volume.
The Purchase Index dropped 0.2% to 157.5 vs. +2.2% to 157.8 a week ago, while the Refinance Index fell 6.2% to 687.3 vs. -1.1% to 732.6 in the previous period.
30-year fixed-rate mortgages rose to 6.85% from 6.79%, the highest since June 2025 and 36 basis points higher than a year ago.
"Mortgage rates moved higher last week, driven by ongoing investor concerns over inflation and the federal budget deficit," said Joel Kan, MBA's vice president and deputy chief economist.

"Refinance applications remain significantly impacted by these higher rates, falling to the slowest weekly pace since May 2025," said Kan. "Higher mortgage rates continue to weigh on prospective homebuyers looking to act, even as housing inventory has increased in many markets."

title: Mortgage demand dips amid higher rates; refinancing activities plunge
